query: The Mock Defence {Final-years run mock defences at the end of the lab. Three in borrowed gowns play the committee, and they play it cruel.|Mock defence day. The pretend committee has added a fourth chair and a tiny gavel.|The mock committee nods at you as you come in. They've started keeping score on the board.} {Tonight's chief examiner is doing an impression of Thorne that is unkindly accurate.|The chair has a bell, which they ring for every "um".|{season == "winter": Everyone defends in scarves; the lab's fire is out.|Someone has borrowed a skeleton from the infirmary to sit in the audience.}} Take the hot seat {You field every question, even the cruel one about your sources. The chief examiner says "Hm," in Thorne's voice, and means it.|They ring the bell for "um" only twice. That's a record, and the committee applauds with the tiny gavel.|You hold your ground for an hour. Your score on the board is the highest of the term, and people come to ask how.} {The third question undoes you. You stand at the board saying "well" while the chief examiner does Thorne's eyebrow at you.|They find the hole in your argument in four minutes, and the bell rings for every "um" after that. Better here than in front of the real thing.|You lose your thread under the gavel. The committee is merciful afterwards, which is worse.} Sit on the committee {You ask one question, quietly, and watch the defender's face as they see the hole. You feel like a cat. A kind cat.|You learn to find the weak joint in an argument by watching three of them crack. It's educational and a little shameful.|You're the committee's favourite examiner now: gentle voice, terrible questions.}
